language_contract.intelligence: Economics for someone who has never heard of this model. No identifiers, no state names, no development history.
language_contract.model: The analytical reasoning: mechanisms, classifications, rivals.

reading.lede: New Mexico's economy is organised around a handful of places that other places depend on, and a public budget funded by a corner of the state that the rest of it cannot see into.
paragraphs: Its labour markets do not follow its county lines. Los Alamos County holds about 18,200 private-sector jobs and roughly 58% of them are filled by people who live elsewhere — mostly Santa Fe, then Bernalillo and Rio Arriba. Torrance County sends 47% of its working residents to Bernalillo. Several northern counties export half their workforce daily and import the income.

Average private earnings at those workplaces differ by a factor of about three and a half across sixty miles — $11,370 a month in Los Alamos against $3,288 in San Miguel. How much of that gap is the same work paid differently, and how much is different work, is not established: these are county averages over different mixes of jobs. What is established is that around 45% of working residents in Rio Arriba and Mora hold jobs outside their county, and that what they earn there is not published.

The state's public finances run the other way. Oil and gas produced in two or three southeastern counties fund a large share of the budget that pays for services everywhere. Where that money finally lands is not published by anyone — which means the largest internal transfer in the state economy cannot be traced to a place.
reading.most_important_unknown: Where state spending lands. Everything else about New Mexico's public economy is downstream of a number nobody publishes.

key_findings.finding: One county supplies jobs for a region, and cannot house the people who fill them.
key_findings.detail: Los Alamos County holds 18,206 private jobs against 7,715 filled by its own residents. About 57.6% commute in.
key_findings.so_what: Employment growth there is a housing and transport question in four other counties, not a business-recruitment question in one.

key_findings.finding: Average earnings at workplaces differ several-fold across short distances, and what explains the gap is not established.
key_findings.detail: Los Alamos $11,370 a month against San Miguel $3,288 — a factor of 3.5. These are county averages over different occupation and industry mixes, so they do not establish that the same work pays differently.
key_findings.so_what: Before treating the gap as an access problem, it is worth knowing whether it is composition. Earnings by occupation within each county would separate the two, and would change which intervention makes sense.

key_findings.finding: The public budget is funded by a corner of the state and spent invisibly across all of it.
key_findings.detail: Oil and gas from the southeast fund a large share of state revenue. No published figure allocates state spending to counties.
key_findings.so_what: Any assessment of what a place receives from the state — or of what it would lose if energy revenue fell — currently rests on nothing.

key_findings.finding: Several counties function as places people live rather than places people work, and the largest case is not in the north.
key_findings.detail: Sandoval sends 59.6% of its working residents to Bernalillo and Valencia 57.0% — larger dependencies than anything in the northern counties. San Miguel 54%, Torrance 73% in total, Mora and Rio Arriba around 45%.
key_findings.so_what: Their labour demand sits in another county. Measuring local business formation there describes a minority of what determines local employment.

key_findings.finding: Where locally generated value ends up is unobservable.
key_findings.detail: $5.28bn of federal work was performed in Los Alamos County in one year; $75M went to recipients registered there. Neither figure says who ultimately received the value.
key_findings.so_what: Retention — the question any regional development strategy turns on — cannot currently be measured anywhere in the state.

earnings.caveat: Measured where the job is, not where the worker lives, and averaged over different mixes of work.

PUBLIC_FINANCE.title: How public money reaches places
PUBLIC_FINANCE.reading: A large share of what New Mexico's government spends is funded by oil and gas produced in two or three southeastern counties. Where that spending finally lands cannot be traced: no published figure allocates state spending to counties. It is the single largest unmeasured relationship in the state's economy.

blind_spots.why_it_matters: It prevents tracing the state's largest internal redistribution. No county can be told what it receives, and no one can estimate what a fall in energy revenue would cost a particular place.

blind_spots.gap: Who owns what, and where the returns go
blind_spots.why_it_matters: Without it, nobody can say whether value generated in a place stays there. It is the question regional development exists to answer and no public source reaches it.

blind_spots.gap: What commuters earn, by the county they live in
blind_spots.why_it_matters: The worker flows are observed; the income they carry home is not. It is the difference between knowing people leave and knowing what their leaving is worth.

blind_spots.gap: Employment and earnings outside nine counties
blind_spots.why_it_matters: Two thirds of New Mexico's counties have no employer-level data here at all, including the energy counties that fund the state.

status.note: A source could answer this; the work of acquiring it has not been done.

investigation.if: housing limits the reach of the Los Alamos labour market
questions: Where do the roughly 10,500 in-commuters actually live, street by street rather than county by county?
How does housing cost compare with earnings by the county workers commute from?
Which commutes are closest to the point where a worker would refuse the job?
investigation.would_settle: whether adding housing, or adding transport, changes who can take these jobs

investigation.if: state spending is the largest untraced flow in the state
questions: What does the capital outlay list show by project location?
Can operating spending be attributed to a county at all, by any agency, for any programme?
investigation.would_settle: whether the fiscal chain can be closed at its last link or whether it is closed only for capital
